thread:
maria (sales): Hey team — CNX corp POC: customer insists on only outbound to their NAT (no inbound). They want to allowlist a set of Redwood egress IPs but are also asking about running a customer-initiated SSH tunnel for logs. Can we confirm options + a quick runbook for onboarding?

alan (solutions): Two patterns we usually propose: 1) Redwood-managed static egress IPs for the Dedicated POC (they allow those IPs in their firewall), or 2) customer-initiated persistent outbound tunnel (keeps connections outbound only). Which do they prefer?

tim (netops): For Dedicated POCs we can allocate up to 3 static EIPs in the region. We need either single IPs or a CIDR from them for our routing table. Note: we terminate TLS at our gateway (443). If they require mutual TLS we can enable client certs at the endpoint.

maria (sales): Security asked for no inbound at all. They prefer outbound-only. They also asked about cert rotation and whether we support client cert auth.

sophie (security): mTLS is optional but recommended for extra assurance. We support client cert validation and have a cert rotation process (automated every 90 days). We can provide a one-page process doc for them. Also: if they will only allow outbound to specific hostnames (SNI), we support SNI routing on our gateway.

alan (solutions): If they truly want zero inbound, the outbound tunnel approach is reliable: a tiny client runs inside their VPC and establishes a persistent TLS tunnel to our relay. That keeps all connections initiated from their side. Behaves like a reverse tunnel but over TLS and with token auth.

tim (netops): Implementation notes for the tunnel: client must allow outbound to relay.redwood.internal:443. Relay authenticates via an API token and presents our cert. For POC we provide a pre-built docker image and a systemd unit example. Example config snippet: 
```
RELAY_HOST=relay.redwood.internal
RELAY_PORT=443
AUTH_TOKEN=redacted-for-demo
```

maria (sales): Pricing question from the buyer: is there an extra fee for static EIP allocation during the POC? Also they asked if reserved capacity is required to hit latency targets.

alan (solutions): Short POC (<=30 days) we typically absorb EIP setup fees. Reserved Dedicated capacity is only needed if they want a production SLA and guaranteed throughput — otherwise shared/burst capacity is fine for evaluation. I'll ping pricing to confirm formal numbers.

sophie (security): Please have them complete the network subsection of our security questionnaire. Key fields we need: allowed_egress_ips, allowed_fqdns (relay hostnames), allowed_ports, client_cert_required boolean, and whether they have an outbound proxy that rewrites headers. I can paste a minimal JSON snippet they can copy.

sophie (security): Snippet to paste: `allowed_egress_ips: ["34.120.55.77"]  allowed_ports: [443]  allowed_fqdns: ["relay.redwood.internal"]  client_cert_required: true|false`

maria (sales): Can we provide a temporary test IP range for initial allowlisting so they can start smoke tests before we allocate final EIPs? Customer wants something ephemeral for 48h.

tim (netops): Yes — we can issue a rotating test IP (/32) valid for 48h for their infra team. For this POC I can provision 34.120.55.77 (TTL 48h). I'll open a ticket and log the allocation in the audit. If they need a small CIDR we'll escalate.

deploy-bot: Ticket #INC-2026 created: "CNX POC - dedicated egress IPs + relay tunnel" assigned to @tim.

maria (sales): Perfect — I'll send the test IP and the minimal network checklist to their infra lead and request the filled questionnaire. Will loop in the customer's infra contact once they respond. :thumbsup:
